On the other hand, it can be interpreted more literally, at which point it seems fantastical to say that an entity (physical or otherwise) could be present everywhere, at every scale of existence, from the micro- to the macro-level. However, entities aren't the only thing that can be omnipresent – processes (a.k.a. interactions) can be, too. In that case, emergence is an example of an omnipresent process of creation whose phenomena exist at distinct levels of organization with their own sets of rules and properties.
